quickAnswer: Acton has few pre-war houses (8.5% from 1939 or earlier, 45th of 50 towns we serve), while 22.5% of its homes sit in buildings of five or more units. Gas heats 55.1% of occupied homes and fuel oil 25.0%, so a replacement job often starts with what is already connected.
body: ## A town built mostly between 1960 and 1979

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 9,170 housing units in Acton. The largest block, 3,525 homes (38.4%), went up between 1960 and 1979, and the median home dates to 1975. Pre-war housing is scarce: only 775 homes (8.5%) are from 1939 or earlier, which ranks Acton 45th of the 50 towns we serve.

That age profile shapes the work. Houses from the 1960 to 1979 stretch were often built with forced-air or baseboard hot-water heat, and insulation standards then were lower than today's. Air sealing, insulation and the condition of any ductwork deserve a look before a new system is sized.

Some much older buildings do survive. The town's history lists the Faulkner Homestead in South Acton, built in 1707 and the oldest home still standing in Acton, and Jones Tavern, a revolutionary-era building on the National Register of Historic Places. A building of that vintage is a very different job from a house of the 1975 era, and the heating plan should reflect it.
## Gas leads, oil follows, electricity trails

Utility gas heats 4,967 occupied homes (55.1%), well above the 41.9% of the middle town. Fuel oil or kerosene heats 2,257 (25.0%), electricity 1,286 (14.3%) and bottled or tank gas 447 (5.0%). Oil is far less common here than in a typical MetroWest town, where the middle figure is 36.5%.

For a failed boiler or furnace, that mix means the first question is what is already connected. A gas home usually wants a like-for-like replacement. An oil home has a choice between a new oil unit, a gas conversion where a main passes the house, and a heat pump. We look at the house before suggesting any of them.
## Larger buildings and renters

Acton is not only single-family streets. Buildings of five or more units hold 2,063 housing units (22.5%), and all multi-unit buildings together hold 2,554 (27.9%), which puts the town 13th of 50. Single-family detached homes are 63.3% of the stock.

The town's history notes that North Acton has had major growth since 1975 to 1980 along the Route 2A/119 corridor, with commercial complexes and condominium buildings. West Acton is the commercial area along Route 111, and the Master Plan encourages development in the village centers to limit sprawl. Condo associations often make shared decisions about boilers, rooftop units and ventilation, and that changes how a replacement is planned and paid for.

Renters live in 2,355 households (26.1%), 12th highest of the 50. Owners of rental housing have to meet the state sanitary code on heat: at least 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight during the heating season.
## Hills, ponds and five village centers

Acton sits on ground the glaciers left behind about ten thousand years ago: nine drumlins (hills of glacial till), kettle ponds such as Wills Hole and Grassy Pond, and two stream systems that drain to the Assabet River. The town has five village centers: Acton Center, West Acton, South Acton, East Acton and North Acton. On any sloped lot, the placement of outdoor condensers and oil tanks is a real design question, and wet, low ground deserves care with basement equipment.
## Value, utility and rebates

Acton's median owner-occupied home is worth $696,500, 15th highest of the 50 towns and well above the $579,150 of the middle town. A home worth more is often worth protecting with correctly sized equipment and good air sealing.

We cannot confirm which electric utility serves every Acton address, so check your bill. Heat pump rebates run through the utility that serves your address, and the amounts are on our [heat pump page](/cities/acton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Is natural gas the most common heat in Acton?
faq.a: Yes. Utility gas heats 55.1% of occupied Acton homes, ahead of fuel oil at 25.0% and electricity at 14.3%. Whether a main runs past your own house depends on the street, so ask during the estimate. The answer decides whether a conversion from oil makes sense, and a free written estimate before work starts lays out the options.

faq.q: Do older Acton houses need special treatment?
faq.a: Only 8.5% of Acton homes date from 1939 or earlier, and 3,525 (38.4%) were built from 1960 to 1979. A very old home, such as the 1707 Faulkner Homestead in South Acton, may have unusual framing and no ducts. We assess the heating load of the specific house before quoting a system.

faq.q: How do condos in Acton handle a boiler replacement?
faq.a: It usually goes through the association, since the equipment may be shared. About 22.5% of Acton homes are in buildings of five or more units. We give a free written estimate before work starts, which a board can review. Ask your management or board early about who owns each piece of equipment.

faq.q: Which utility sets my heat pump rebate in Acton?
faq.a: The utility that serves your address. We have not confirmed it for every Acton home, so check your electric bill, then confirm current terms at masssave.com or with your utility, because terms can change. Mass Save's 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Utility gas heats 4,967 Acton homes and fuel oil heats 2,257, so most boiler and furnace calls begin as either a gas swap or an oil decision. Gas equipment also brings a permit and an inspection into the job.
body: ## Gas swap or oil decision

Acton ranks 15th of 50 towns for utility gas and 36th for fuel oil. Gas is the default here: 4,967 occupied homes, or 55.1%, against 2,257 (25.0%) on oil or kerosene. The two groups face different questions when a heating plant fails.
### Gas homes

A gas household usually replaces what it has, so the useful questions are about size and venting. The median Acton house dates to 1975, and 1,267 homes were built from 1940 to 1959. Insulation, windows and attic air sealing in houses of those ages may have been improved since the original boiler went in, which can leave the old output rating too large. Ask for a heating-load figure before accepting a like-for-like size.
### Oil homes

An oil household faces a real fork. The choices are a new oil boiler or furnace, a move to gas where a main runs past the lot, or a heat pump with the old unit kept as backup. With 2,257 homes on oil, the question comes up often, and the right answer depends on the house, not on the town average.
### Permit and inspection

Gas equipment is regulated work. In Massachusetts only licensed plumbers and gas fitters can pull the gas permit, and a new furnace or boiler normally ends with a final inspection. The town's building department can say what it needs for your address.
### Bottled gas and wood

Bottled gas heats 447 Acton homes (5.0%) and wood heats 45. Those fuels are bought rather than piped in, so a failed boiler on a cold night is a time-sensitive call. Our line at (508) 786-8755 is open around the clock.
### Older stock

Across the town, 5,567 homes (60.7%) were built before 1980. In houses of that vintage, the age of the distribution (pipes, radiators, ducts) matters as much as the age of the boiler. For scheduled care, see the [maintenance page](/cities/acton/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Is gas or oil more common for heating in Acton?
faq.a: Gas is far more common. Utility gas heats 55.1% of occupied Acton homes and fuel oil or kerosene heats 25.0%. Electricity heats 14.3%. Which one applies to your own house depends on what is connected today, and that fact drives whether the job is a straight replacement or a larger comparison of options.

faq.q: Can an Acton oil boiler be converted to gas?
faq.a: Sometimes. It depends on whether a gas main reaches the street and whether the utility will connect the house. If it does, the conversion is a gas-fitter job with a permit and inspection. If it does not, the realistic choices are new oil equipment or a heat pump, and we can lay out each side by side.

faq.q: Why does house age matter when sizing a new boiler or furnace in Acton?
faq.a: The median Acton home was built in 1975, and 60.7% predate 1980. Older houses may have gained insulation or new windows since their first boiler, so the old nameplate size can overshoot today's need. A heating-load assessment before the quote is the way to check, rather than copying the old unit.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Acton has 5,809 detached houses, 791 townhouses and 2,554 units in multi-unit buildings, and each type is cooled differently. We match central air, ductless or a heat pump to the building, not to a template.
body: ## Cooling by building type

The ACS 2022 counts 5,809 single-family detached homes in Acton (63.3%) and 791 attached townhouses (8.6%). Buildings with two units hold 258 homes and buildings with three or four units hold 233. The largest multi-unit group is the 2,063 units (22.5%) in buildings of five or more.
### Detached houses

Where a forced-air furnace already moves air through ducts, a central air conditioner may be able to share them, provided the ducts are the right size and in good shape. Many older houses were built without central air at all. A house heated by hot-water baseboards has no ducts, and the usual routes are ductless heads or a small-duct system.
### Townhouses

Attached homes share walls, so an outdoor unit has to fit inside the lot and the neighbors' tolerance for noise. A ductless system puts the compressor outside and the quiet part inside. Check any association rules before choosing a spot.
### Condominium buildings

With 27.9% of Acton's homes in multi-unit buildings, the town ranks 13th of 50 for that share. The median of the 50 towns is 16.1%. In a large building, rooftop or shared equipment may belong to the association, so the first call is often to the board or property manager.
### Sizing for the site

Oversized equipment cools fast, shuts off early and leaves the air clammy. Sizing from the house itself (insulation, window area, shade from trees) is steadier. The load calculation is done for the building in front of us, not copied from the unit it replaces.
### One system for both seasons

A heat pump cools in summer and heats in winter, and it can replace an older cooling-only unit. See the [heat pump page](/cities/acton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) for how that decision looks in Acton.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to an Acton house that has baseboard heat?
faq.a: Yes. Baseboard hot water has no ducts, so a ductless mini-split is the usual answer. Each indoor head serves one room or zone and connects to an outdoor unit by a small line set. A visit can show how many heads your layout needs, and where the outdoor unit can sit without blocking drainage.

faq.q: Do condo owners in Acton need approval for an outdoor unit?
faq.a: Often yes. Condominium documents commonly control where equipment can go and how it looks, and 22.5% of Acton homes sit in buildings of five or more units. Read the documents and talk with the board before choosing a location, since approval can take longer than the installation itself.

faq.q: Is a weak air conditioner always a replacement job?
faq.a: No. A unit that cools poorly may need a repair, and a compressor failure on aging equipment is the case that usually points to replacement. We put the repair option and the replacement option in writing so you can compare them, and we also ask whether a heat pump would fit the house better.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Acton has 1,286 electric-heat homes, 2,257 on oil and 447 on bottled gas, a large pool of households comparing heat pumps with their current system. Which rebate applies turns on who supplies the electricity at each address.
body: ## Who in Acton has the most to compare

We have not confirmed the electric supplier for Acton addresses, and incentives follow that supplier. The 2026 whole-home amount is $2,650 per ton up to $8,500, and the full rules are on our [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### The fuel mix

Oil heats 2,257 Acton homes and bottled gas heats 447. Those households buy fuel by delivery, so a cold-climate heat pump is worth pricing against a replacement boiler. Electricity already heats 1,286 homes (14.3%), ranking Acton 15th of 50 for that share. Where that electric heat is baseboard resistance, a heat pump moves the same heat with less electricity. The 55.1% of homes on utility gas face a different comparison, since a heat pump may be added for cooling rather than to replace the furnace.
### Age bands and the weatherization test

A whole-home rebate asks that the house first count as weatherized, and one of the three ways is a build year of 2000 or later. In Acton that group is 1,579 homes (17.2%). The 2,024 homes from 1980 to 1999 and the 3,525 from 1960 to 1979 would need an assessment or earlier work to qualify, and the 5,567 homes built before 1980 are the group where an insulation visit is most likely to come first.
### Housing type decides ducted or ductless

Of Acton's housing units, 63.3% are detached houses, 8.6% townhouses and 27.9% in multi-unit buildings. A detached house with good ducts can take a ducted system. A baseboard house, an addition or a condominium unit often suits ductless heads, one per zone. A mixed house can use both.
### Keeping the boiler as backup
An oil house can retire the boiler or keep it as a cold-snap backup beside the heat pump. That is a partial-home setup, and the rebate for it is smaller than the whole-home one.
### Sizing comes first
The load assessment comes before any quote, and the equipment size follows from it. For cooling-only questions, see the [air conditioning page](/cities/acton/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: Which utility sets my heat pump rebate in Acton?
faq.a: Whichever company supplies your electricity, and we have not confirmed that for every Acton home. Your bill names it. Then check current terms with that company and at masssave.com, since they can change. The answer decides which program applies, so it is worth settling before you compare quotes.

faq.q: Can my Acton oil house keep the boiler and add a heat pump?
faq.a: Yes. A partial-home setup lets the heat pump handle most of the year and the boiler cover the coldest stretch. With 2,257 oil homes in town, the question is common. The trade-off is that you still maintain the oil system, and the rebate is smaller than for a whole-home installation.

faq.q: Does a heat pump in Acton need ductwork?
faq.a: No. Ductless mini-splits work without ducts, using an indoor head in each zone, which suits baseboard houses and additions. A ducted system makes sense when the house already has ducts in good condition. In a mixed house, one part can be ducted and another ductless, planned from the heating load of the whole building.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Acton has 6,666 owner households and 2,355 renter households, with gas, oil, electric and bottled gas all in use. The right tune-up depends on the fuel, so we start by asking what the equipment burns or draws.
body: ## Care that follows the fuel
Acton splits into 6,666 owner-occupied households (73.9%) and 2,355 renter-occupied ones (26.1%). The fuels differ too, so the checklist does as well.
### Oil, 2,257 homes

An oil burner and its boiler or furnace need a cleaning every year. Many technicians change the nozzle and filter and test combustion at the same visit. Skipping a year lets soot build up, which can lead to a breakdown in the coldest weeks.
### Utility gas, 4,967 homes
A gas check covers the burner, heat exchanger, venting and controls, with carbon monoxide testing. It is the safety visit as much as the efficiency one.
### Electric and heat pump, 1,286 homes

Coil cleaning, filter changes, a look at the refrigerant side and a check of the outdoor unit cover most of it. A mini-split has a filter in each indoor head, so a house with several heads has several filters.
### Bottled gas, 447 homes
Same as gas, plus a look at the tank, regulator and piping.
### Shared buildings

Acton has 2,063 units in buildings of five or more. Where equipment is shared, a service schedule agreed with the board or manager heads off the cold-night emergency. A landlord who services before the season is spared a midwinter call.
### A calendar that fits New England

Heating checks belong in late summer or early autumn, before the first frost. Cooling and mini-split checks belong in spring. A noise, a smell, short cycling or a jump in the bill is a reason to call at any time of year.
### What to have ready

Bring the fuel, the approximate age of the unit, the make and model on the nameplate and a description of what you noticed. For replacement questions, see the [heating page](/cities/acton/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should an Acton oil system be serviced?
faq.a: Once a year, ahead of the heating season. With 25.0% of Acton homes on oil, the annual visit is one of the most common jobs. It keeps soot from building up and gives the technician a chance to spot a worn part while the weather is still mild.

faq.q: Is a yearly check worth it for a gas furnace in Acton?
faq.a: Usually yes. A yearly look at the burner, venting and heat exchanger can catch safety problems early, and carbon monoxide testing is part of it. A clean system also tends to run more steadily through a long cold spell. Utility gas heats 4,967 homes in town, so this is the most common kind of visit.

faq.q: What can I do between visits?
faq.a: Change the filter on schedule, keep space clear around the equipment and keep outdoor units free of leaves and snow. Check thermostat settings and batteries before you call. These steps do not replace a professional visit, but they remove several simple causes of no-heat and weak-cooling calls.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Acton's housing runs from 775 homes built in 1939 or earlier to 613 built since 2010, with 3,525 from 1960 to 1979 in between. Each age band tends to bring its own air-quality questions, so we start with how the house breathes.
body: ## Air quality by age band

The ACS 2022 puts Acton's housing into clear bands: 775 homes from 1939 or earlier (8.5%), 1,267 from 1940 to 1959, 3,525 from 1960 to 1979, 2,024 from 1980 to 1999 and 1,579 from 2000 on. Since 2010, 613 homes have been added. Each band tends to have its own air problems.
### Homes built before 1980

Older houses are often leaky enough to exchange air on their own. Natural leakage thins out some indoor pollutants, but it also brings in outdoor dust and pollen. With 5,567 Acton homes in this group, sealing and ventilation are choices to weigh together, not separately. Before a gut renovation in an older building, ask a qualified specialist to test the old materials.
### Newer and tighter homes

A house built since 2000 is usually tighter. That saves energy and also keeps cooking fumes, moisture and furnishing chemicals indoors unless ventilation does its job. In those homes the first things to check are the bath fans and the range hood exhaust. Acton has 1,579 homes in this newer group.
### Basements and wet ground

Acton's landscape includes nine drumlins, kettle ponds and brooks. A damp basement has a source: groundwater, a pipe, or warm summer air condensing on cool masonry. A dehumidifier manages the symptom only, so find the source before buying one.
### Shared walls

In the 2,554 units in multi-unit buildings, cooking smells, smoke and moisture can travel between units. Sealing gaps and balancing ventilation help, and each unit may need its own filter and fan settings.
### Ducts
Duct cleaning is a niche call for ducts with visible mold, heavy dirt or renovation debris. Otherwise we start with the filter and the airflow.
### Filters and upkeep
Filter changes and seasonal checks do much of the work of keeping air clean. See the [maintenance page](/cities/acton/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Do I need my Acton ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. Cleaning is for ducts with visible mold, heavy dirt or renovation debris. Otherwise the money is often better spent on a better filter, sealing leaks or fixing a moisture source. We look at the ducts and the filter, then say what we would do.

faq.q: Why is the air in my Acton basement damp?
faq.a: Damp comes from groundwater, from a leaking pipe or from humid summer air meeting cool masonry. A dehumidifier treats the air but not the cause, so any leak or poor drainage still needs its own repair. A plumber or a drainage contractor may be the right first call.

faq.q: Does a tighter newer home need ventilation?
faq.a: Often, yes. A house built in 2000 or later is usually tighter, so cooking fumes, moisture and chemicals from furnishings stay inside unless fans and ventilation move them out. Check that the bathroom fan runs and the range hood vents outdoors. If the air still feels stale, a ventilation addition to the system is the next option.
